text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak Interior Minister Gustav Krajci is on a three-day visit to Russia to negotiate supplies of Russian special equipment for Slovak police and further repayment of Russian debts to Slovakia through deliveries of military aircraft.

- Opposition Democratic Union (DU) Deputy and Former Finance Minister Rudolf Filkus said the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), will have liquidity problems due to the maturation of privatisation bonds in 2001.
- The Slovak branch of Germany's Hypo-Bank said it had requested a licence for providing loans in Slovakia.
- University students said they were considering a protest strike if the governemnt rejects their proposal to start a dialogue over the controversial university law.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Bankers warn that the new foreign exchange position, a central bank measure aimed at curbing the extension of loans in hard currencies, will weaken competitivenes of domestic banks against the foreign financial institutions.

- Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa and a group of Croatian businessmen are expected to visit Slovakia's largest steel producer VSZ in December to discuss possible mutual cooperation, especially between VSZ and Croatian harbours.

SME - HBD Slovakia, a private printing company, said it would appeal to the Constituional Court against the controversial banbkruptcy law which prevents state companies from going into liquidation. HBD said the law's only purpose was to protect state telephone monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie which, HBD says, owes it more than 100 billion crowns.
